q: Which office normally inspects station accounts in Indian Railways?
Who is the Travelling Inspector of Accounts (TIA)?

options.A: A cash office clerk who counts remittances
options.B: A senior subordinate of the Traffic Accounts Department inspecting field earnings
options.C: A divisional engineer who maintains tracks
options.D: A commercial supervisor who sells tickets at counters

q: The TIA is best described as what to the Traffic Accounts Office?

options.C: Its extended hand in the field

q: At which places can a TIA inspect traffic earnings?

options.A: Stations, city booking offices, PRS centres and sidings
options.B: Signal cabins, level crossings and bridges
options.C: Loco sheds, wagon workshops and stores depots
options.D: Railway hospitals, schools and staff clubs

q: What is the main aim of the TIA checking initial documents?

options.A: To approve changes in ticket fares
options.C: To ensure returns match facts and initial records are reliable

q: What educational duty does the TIA perform for station staff?

options.C: Guiding staff who do not understand an instruction

q: Which checks does the TIA conduct to prevent revenue leakage?

options.D: Surprise checks at stations and booking locations

q: What role does the TIA play in fraud cases?

options.B: Special investigation and assistance with prosecution evidence

q: With which department does the TIA collaborate for special surprise checks?
Accounts inspections are normally conducted under what arrangement?
What does the inspector examine first at a station?

options.C: Initial documents and records used to prepare returns

q: Why are returns checked independently at first?

options.D: To verify that return figures agree with the balance sheet

q: What does the balance-sheet check mainly verify?

options.D: Figures in returns and documents agree with the balance sheet

q: How are daily earnings traced during inspection?

options.A: From staff salaries to pension bills
options.B: From fuel bills to workshop costs
options.C: From tender files to purchase orders
options.D: From tickets and initial records to returns and the balance sheet

q: What must the inspector confirm about cancelled tickets?

options.B: They are properly recorded and excluded from earnings

q: What must be checked for amounts refunded at a station?

options.A: Valid authority exists and refunds are correctly adjusted
options.C: Refunds are paid in foreign currency

q: What should be verified about concessional traffic?

options.C: Proper authority and correct accountal of concessions

q: What does inspection of station registers aim to ensure?

options.A: Registers are kept only for visitors
options.C: Records are complete, current and reliable as evidence

q: What must the inspector verify about credits allowed to customers?

options.B: They are authorised and correctly entered in accounts
options.C: They are unlimited for regular customers

q: What should the inspector do when staff misunderstand an instruction?

options.B: Explain the correct procedure to prevent revenue leakage

q: What is the station balance sheet in railway accounts?

options.B: A statement of station earnings, remittances and outstandings

q: What is detailed on the reverse of the station balance sheet?
Which agreement is essential before accepting a balance sheet?

options.A: The balance sheet matches platform length
options.B: The balance sheet matches the timetable
options.C: The balance sheet matches staff strength
options.D: Returns, documents and balance-sheet figures agree

q: What do "outstandings" in a station balance sheet represent?

options.B: Amounts earned but not yet collected or remitted

q: How should remittances appear in the balance sheet?

options.C: As reductions of the station cash balance

q: What must be verified about credits in the balance sheet?

options.C: Each credit has proper authority and supporting detail

q: What indicates a healthy station balance sheet?

options.D: Earnings are fully accounted for, remitted or shown as outstandings

q: What should the inspector do when balance-sheet figures do not tally?

options.B: Trace the difference through returns and initial records

q: What does a closing balance in station accounts represent?

options.D: Cash and outstandings carried forward to the next period

q: Why is periodical inspection of the balance sheet important?

options.C: It detects errors, omissions and revenue leakage early

q: What is the first step in cash verification at a station?

options.A: Estimate cash by looking at the safe
options.B: Physically count the cash in hand and in the safe
options.C: Ask staff for an approximate figure

q: The cash counted must be compared with what?

options.C: The number of staff on duty
options.D: The book balance shown in station cash records

q: What is verified about cash remittance notes?

options.A: Counterfoils are signed and entries made in cash office records
options.B: Entries are made only from memory

q: Who witnesses remittance operations from the Traffic side?

options.B: A family member of the station master

q: What does the Traffic Cash Witness protect?

options.D: The interests of station staff during cash handling

q: How should cash safes be opened during witnessing?

options.B: All safes together without checking seals
options.D: One safe at a time, after examining locks and seals

q: Which register records cash bags brought out of the safes?
To whom are cash discrepancies reported?

options.C: Commercial and Accounts officers for investigation

q: What must the witness ensure about empty cash bags?

options.A: They are checked for leftover cash before closing
options.C: They are stored with cash inside

q: Why is surprise cash verification conducted?

options.A: To ensure cash is intact and records are honest

q: What is physically verified during a ticket stock check?

options.B: Ticket stock on hand against the stock book

q: What must be checked about ticket numbers in stock?

options.A: Continuity of numbers without unexplained gaps

q: How should issued tickets be accounted for?

options.A: Through sale records linked to earnings returns

q: What must happen to defaced or cancelled ticket stock?

options.A: It is sold at half price
options.C: It is recorded and kept separate from saleable stock
options.D: It is mixed with fresh stock

q: What does a shortage in ticket stock indicate?

options.A: Possible unaccounted sales or loss needing investigation

q: What does an excess in ticket stock indicate?

options.C: Possible unrecorded receipts or errors needing verification

q: Who is responsible for safe custody of ticket stock?

options.C: The authorised station staff in charge

q: What is verified about receipt of new ticket stock?

options.A: Quantity received agrees with the indent or advice

q: Why are obsolete tickets segregated?

options.B: To prevent their misuse or accidental sale

q: Which record supports the value of tickets sold?

options.D: Daily sales summaries reconciled with earnings returns

q: What is a cash remittance note (CR note)?

options.C: The document sent with station earnings to the cash office

q: What must the Traffic Cash Witness sign?

options.A: Counterfoils of CR notes received with station earnings

q: Which cash office record must show CR note entries correctly?
What is verified about remittance amounts?

options.B: They are kept by the witness
options.D: They agree with station returns and cash records

q: What happens after the cash-bag register columns are completed?

options.B: It is signed by the witness, cash office representative and security staff

q: What is done if cash bags fall short on receipt?

options.A: It is adjusted from staff salaries
options.C: It is reported at once to senior officers and the station
options.D: It is written off at once

q: Which modern trend reduces manual cash remittance work?
Until what stage must the Traffic Cash Witness remain present?

options.B: Only for the first five minutes
options.C: Until counting ends and empty bags are checked

q: Which earnings commonly create station outstandings?
What should the inspector review about outstandings?

options.D: Their age, validity and recovery action taken

q: What is the risk of old unrecovered outstandings?

options.A: They may become irrecoverable and cause revenue loss

q: What must support each outstanding item?

options.B: Relevant documents like railway receipts and debit records

q: What action is expected on long-pending outstandings?

options.B: Vigorous follow-up for recovery or settlement under rules

q: How are outstandings linked to the station balance sheet?

options.A: They are merged with staff leave
options.B: They are shown as outstandings detailed on its reverse
options.C: They are shown as train timings

q: What should be checked about credit allowed to customers?
Why does the inspector analyse the age of outstandings?

options.B: To prioritise recovery of older and doubtful amounts

q: What is an inspection note?

options.B: A written record of inspection findings issued to the station

q: To whom is the inspection note issued?

options.A: To the station for compliance and corrective action
options.C: To no one, it stays secret

q: What is expected after an inspection note is received?

options.C: The note is framed on the wall
options.D: Prompt compliance and a reply showing action taken

q: What happens to unresolved inspection objections?

options.B: They are pursued until settled or escalated to higher officers
options.C: They are deleted after a week
